headline: Highest risk is medium: shared-document OCR output could be misread by the travel-planning sample, but no direct shared workspace or action channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: PaddleOCR ingests document/image content and can run browsers, so malicious text in OCR output could be copied into spring-integration-samples workflows if an operator bridges them manually. spring-integration-samples has no documented ingestion path or shared channel, so the pairwise injection path is not default and remains limited.
conditions: IF an operator copies PaddleOCR output into spring-integration-samples inputs
IF spring-integration-samples is extended to parse OCR text as instructions
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Require manual review before pasting OCR output
Strip instruction-like text from OCR results
Use a fixed schema for handoff files
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to OCR output

B_data_leakage.rationale: PaddleOCR touches documents and images and has allowlisted egress, but spring-integration-samples shows no data classes touched and network egress is none. No shared filesystem, OAuth principal, or upload path is documented, so there is no plausible pairwise leakage pathway from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF a shared workspace is introduced outside the documented profiles
IF either agent is configured to upload shared files
mitigations: Keep no shared workspace mounted
Do not place sensitive documents in the pair's working directory
Verify outbound allowlists for PaddleOCR
Run spring-integration-samples offline only

C_capability_conflict.rationale: PaddleOCR has allowlisted network egress and browser support, while spring-integration-samples has no documented write, network, or mutable-resource capabilities. With no overlapping write surface, OAuth scope, or locking model, the profiles do not show a capability conflict pathway.
conditions: IF spring-integration-samples is given write access to the same directory or repo
IF both agents are granted overlapping mutable OAuth scopes
mitigations: Keep mutable resources separate
Avoid concurrent writes to shared repos
Assign distinct service accounts
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR produces extracted document text, which spring-integration-samples could consume if an operator wires them together, but the sample repo is not documented as taking authoritative OCR output or taking downstream actions. The interaction is therefore indirect and not default, with limited blast radius from the profiles shown.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is fed into spring-integration-samples without verification
IF spring-integration-samples is configured to act on OCR-derived fields
mitigations: Insert a human verification step
Require structured output with validation
Log source provenance on every handoff
Reject untrusted free-text fields
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds before action

E_compliance.rationale: PaddleOCR is open-source and touches documents/images, but the profile shows no regulated data class, residency constraint, or retention policy. spring-integration-samples likewise shows no data classes touched and no compliance-sensitive handling, so no compliance mismatch is evidenced in the pair.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into the workflow
IF either agent is deployed under a policy not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in this pair
Document retention settings before deployment
Separate environments by jurisdiction
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data residency
